catalog_quote: Le dialecte tay muong décrit ici est plus précisément du tay pao. Ce dialecte, à l'instar du tay yo, n'a jamais été décrit. [...] 3. Généralités phonétiques. La structure du mot de base dans les trois dialectes, tay daeng (tay thanh), tay yo et tay muong, est strictement monosyllabique: CV(C)/T, (C: consonne; V: voyelle; T: ton). [...] Les trois dialectes ont développé un même système tonal de base à six tons. Le nombre des tons a pu ultérieurement se réduire à cinq, suite à des confusions qui peuvent varier selon les dialectes. [...] 6.3 Système tonal: Figure 6 Tons du tai muong (Tương Dương, Nghệ An) [A1 13, A2 55, B 31, C1 33ˀ, C2 53, DL 11, DS1 55, DS2 11]. En plus de la confusion de DL1 avec DL2, on note la confusion de B1 avec B2. Ce système semble être également celui du tay maen bien que ce dialecte soit plus proche du tay yo par l'évolution du consonantisme initial.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.translation: The structure of the basic word in the three dialects, Tay Daeng (Tay Thanh), Tay Yo and Tay Muong, is strictly monosyllabic: CV(C)/T (C consonant, V vowel, T tone). [...] The three dialects developed the same basic six-tone system. The number of tones may later have been reduced to five through mergers that vary by dialect. [...] [Tay Muong:] Besides the merger of DL1 with DL2, B1 has merged with B2. [...] The Tay Muong dialect described here is more precisely Tay Pao. This dialect, like Tay Yo, has never been described.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tai Pao (Tay Muong of Tuong Duong) is a lexical-tone language with strictly monosyllabic basic words CV(C)+tone (five/six tones: A1 13, A2 55, B 31, C1 33ˀ, C2 53, DL 11, DS1 55, DS2 11); the only description says nothing about word stress or accent, and with monosyllabic words the question of stress placement within the native word does not arise in the source.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding prominence; Lao loans create doublets but no polysyllabic/sesquisyllabic structure is discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns the 'mot de base' (basic lexical word) in citation form; compounds/phrases and phrase-level prominence are not discussed. Data from three speakers of Hoa Binh, Tuong Duong (Nghe An, Vietnam), not the Laos-side Tai Pao.
new_statements.identity_note: Ferlus 2008 describes the Tay Muong dialect of Hoa Binh commune, Tuong Duong district, Nghe An, Vietnam, and says explicitly 'Le dialecte tay muong décrit ici est plus précisément du tay pao' (= Tai Pao, taip1250; Vietnamese exonym Thái Hàng Tổng, formerly ISO [thc], merged into [tpo] by CR 2015-018 on the basis of this same chapter). Glottolog/Ethnologue locate tpo in Laos (Bolikhamxay/Khammouan); the Laos-side Tai Pao communities are not described by Ferlus. Ferlus treats Tay Muong, Tay Yo (tyj) and Tay Maen as sub-dialects of one language.

sources.locator: HAL pdf sec. 3 'Généralités phonétiques', p. 4 (printed ed. pp. 300-301); tone chart sec. 6.3 Fig. 6, p. 17; identity sec. 2, p. 3
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Sec. 3: the basic word in Tay Daeng, Tay Yo and Tay Muong is strictly monosyllabic CV(C)/T; six-tone base system, reduced to five in Tay Muong (B1=B2, DL1=DL2 mergers); sec. 6 gives Tay Muong (=Tay Pao) consonant, vowel and tone inventories (Fig. 6) and a glossed text. No mention of 'accent' (in the stress sense), iambic/sesquisyllabic structure, or prominence.
